3) VAT: legal prefers to insert "Customer is responsible for taxes, duties and VAT unless Redwood is required by law to collect VAT" — Marissa, pls confirm if we can standardize on that wording or if Finance wants Redwood to collect VAT for EU invoices.
4) Minimum commit / cadence: Ben, can you produce a one-line mapping from commit tranches to invoice cadence (monthly/quarterly/prepay)? That can be included in an order-form appendix.

- Today: commercial confirmation (Ben) + legal tax language (Marissa)

- Friday: if both sides agree, prep DocuSign envelope for the order form

Adding the commercial view — I ran the numbers with pricing ops. Quick notes:

- Minimum commit mapping: 0-50k monthly -> billed monthly, 50k-250k -> quarterly invoicing with prepay option, 250k+ -> annual prepay / tranche invoice. I'll attach a short spreadsheet showing invoice cadence per commit tranche.
- Net terms: we can accept Net45 for recurring invoices. For onboarding/activation fees we typically ask Net30; to preserve cashflow, propose an early-pay 2% within 10 days discount as an incentive if procurement pushes Net45 for everything.
- Taxes: commercial prefers Redwood not to own VAT unless required. If Finvera's EU entity invoices locally, they should handle VAT; if Redwood is the collecting entity for EU usage we need to enable VAT registration and remit, which increases complexity and delay.

Next step: Marissa, can legal prepare the redline with the proposed tax clause and a short note on invoicing entity options so we can send a single consolidated reply?

Thanks,

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Draft order form — legal redlines attached

Folks — attaching a legal redline (Finvera_OrderForm_redlines_v3.pdf) with the following key changes and rationale:

1) Taxes: replace ambiguous language with: "Customer shall be responsible for all taxes, duties or similar governmental assessments (other than Redwood's income taxes). Where Redwood is required by applicable law to collect VAT, Customer will reimburse Redwood for such VAT. If Customer provides valid tax-exemption documentation, Redwood will not charge such taxes." This preserves our position while allowing collection where necessary.
2) Invoice entity: add a short "Invoice Recipient" appendix: Customer to specify invoice recipient per PO. If Customer requests Redwood to change remit-to entity after signature, require 30 days' notice and a change-order acceptance by Redwood Finance.
3) Minimum commit: clarified definition of "minimum committed spend" and added a 60-day cure window for measurement disputes before charging catch-up invoices.
4) Net terms: agreed to Net45 on recurring, asked Finance to review upfront activation Net30 vs Net45 exception.

I also included a redline to the signature and acceptance flow to ensure we do not prematurely bind the MSA for future addenda. If Procurement (Finvera) wants Redwood to be the VAT collecting entity in EU, we need to scope VAT registration and we will add a 60–90 day lead time and potential pass-through fee to cover administrative costs.

Attaching: Finvera_OrderForm_redlines_v3.pdf

-Marissa
